title: ATSB / REPCON: no-blame investigation culture and confidential reporting for transport safety concerns
summary: ATSB/REPCON is encoded to preserve the connection between no-blame investigation philosophy and confidential reporting: free flow of safety information is treated as a design requirement, and REPCON allows safety concerns to be de-identified and routed for action.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0007 as a source-infrastructure record for the near-miss / signal-capture lane.

claims.claim: ATSB frames its work as improving aviation, marine, and rail safety through independent no-blame investigation, safety data recording, analysis, research, and influence on safety action.
what_would_change_status: ATSB changes mission, statutory status, or relation to regulators/operators.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: ATSB states that its investigations do not apportion blame or determine liability and that seeking to lay blame would compromise the future free flow of safety information; it adds that the no-blame approach supports cooperation and reporting.
what_would_change_status: ATSB legislation or policy changes the no-blame investigation model.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: REPCON is an ATSB voluntary confidential reporting scheme that allows anyone with an aviation safety concern to report confidentially, with protection of the reporter’s identity and named individuals as a primary element.
what_would_change_status: ATSB changes REPCON eligibility or confidentiality terms.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: REPCON reportable concerns include incidents, circumstances, procedures, practices, or conditions affecting safety; examples include bypassing safety procedures because of operational or commercial pressures. REPCON processing de-identifies text, forwards it to a relevant organisation, and may issue information briefs or alerts.
what_would_change_status: ATSB changes reportable concern examples or processing pathways.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional HTML extraction; no outcome evaluation or database sampling yet
limitations: This record establishes infrastructure existence, stated purpose, and reported process; it does not estimate effectiveness, representativeness, underreporting, or downstream safety impact.
No reporter narratives are imported in rev0007; privacy and de-identification boundaries are preserved.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: Australia; ATSB transport modes broadly, with rev0007 REPCON extraction focused on aviation page
signal_capture_model: information brief or alert when appropriate
reporter_protection_design: no-blame investigation posture to preserve free-flow information
outputs: REPCON information briefs or alert bulletins
limitations: REPCON page extracted is aviation-specific, not full marine/rail REPCON extraction
does not evaluate actual safety actions or confidentiality history
not anonymous: scheme requires contactable reporter
type_payload.query_value: Provides a jurisdictional contrast where no-blame investigation theory and confidential reporting are visibly connected in official source language.

handling_notes: Do not attempt to re-identify reporters or named parties from confidential/de-identified reporting systems.
Infrastructure records are not evidence that all weak signals were handled well or that a reporting system prevented a specific accident.
Preserve distinction among mandatory reporting, voluntary self-reporting, confidential concern reporting, accident investigation, and recommendation tracking.

unknowns: Quantitative uptake, underreporting, signal quality, follow-through rates, and confidentiality failure history are not extracted yet.
No sample of individual reports, alerts, recommendations, or closed actions has been coded yet.
next_actions: Add database/export sampling plan and legal/ethical handling rules before importing any de-identified report narratives.
Add outcome or follow-through records showing when a report led to action, when it did not, and when confidentiality or reporting incentives failed.
Cross-link with warning-governance cases only when a source shows a specific relation; do not infer relation from infrastructure existence.
